title: positive wording
rule: Use positive wording; avoid negatives that force users to reverse the statement (especially opt-in checkboxes).

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Statements (esp. opt-in checkboxes) are positive; checking means agreement with a direct statement.
fail_when: User must reverse a negative (e.g. “don’t not email me”) to opt in or out.
overview: Phrase statements positively so checking means agreement, not a double negative.
apply_when: Writing opt-in checkboxes and other agree/disagree form statements.
not_when: Legal prohibitions that must stay negative to stay accurate.
agent_hint: Word opt-ins positively; avoid negatives that force users to reverse the statement.
description: Use positive wording and avoid negatives that force users to reverse the statement, especially on opt-in checkboxes. Checking should mean agreement with a direct statement, not decoding a double negative. Apply when writing agree/disagree and opt-in copy. Fail patterns where the user must reverse a negative — for example “don’t not email me” — to opt in or out.
